_README: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for which companies get found, which person at each company gets the connection request, and what the note says. This is the SHIPPED DEFAULT. The live, user-edited copy is outreach_config.json (gitignored). Both skills load the live config at the START of every run - scheduled or on-demand - and use ONLY these values. To retarget, follow RETARGETING.md, which edits the live outreach_config.json. Never edit knob values inline in the skills; edit them here.
campaign_label: Job search networking - Data/Analytics roles, Europe, remote-friendly

finder.search_keywords_label: Data Analyst, Data Extraction Specialist, Web Scraping Specialist, Analytics Engineer, BI Developer, Power BI Developer, Business Intelligence Analyst, SQL Analyst, Data Engineer
finder.search_mode_label: companies currently hiring for one of these keywords
finder.job_titles_label: Data Analyst, Product Analyst, Business Analyst, BI Analyst, Reporting Analyst (refined from your CV)
finder.job_markets_label: Worldwide-remote, EMEA and Europe (US-only listings are skipped - they need US residency)
finder.job_posted_within_label: Posted in the last 3 days (already-seen jobs are skipped)
finder.jobs_per_run_label: Up to 10 new jobs per morning run (2 contacts each = 20 requests, the daily cap)
finder.job_pages_per_run_label: Open at most 20 job postings per run, 4-9 s apart (rate-limit protection)
finder.candidate_country_label: Not set yet - your country of residence (from your CV)
finder.work_authorization: Remote only. No visa sponsorship and no relocation. Can work as an employee of a global/EOR employer or as a contractor (B2B) from candidate_country.
finder.work_authorization_label: Remote only - no sponsorship, no relocation
eligibility_reject_phrases: authorized to work in the United States
right to work in the UK
finder.eligibility_flexible_label: Single-country listings that say 'location of your choice' etc. are kept, flagged 'check before applying'
finder.cv_profile_label: Not set yet - filled in from your CV
finder.min_cv_fit: Keep a job only if the CV covers most of its must-have skills (tools like SQL / Python / Power BI and the seniority level). Nice-to-haves do not count against it.

persona_tiers.who: Technical Recruiter, Talent Acquisition Partner, People/Talent team member - verified to recruit for data, analytics or tech roles (headline, About, or recent posts), not just any recruiter at the company

The person directly above the role you'd fill: Head of Data, Head of BI, Data/Analytics Manager, Analytics Engineering Manager, Lead Data Analyst, Director/VP of Data - check acronyms too (BI, VP, Dir.)
Founder, Co-founder or CTO - use at companies under the small-company threshold, where there is no dedicated data lead yet

outreach.personas_per_company_label: 1 person per company (recruiter first, hiring manager as fallback)
outreach.note_char_limit_label: 200 characters max per connection note (counting spaces)
outreach.note_tone: Proactive, not passive: name the specific angle that made you reach out - a career transition, a project, a skill, the exact role they're hiring for - and say plainly that it stood out to you. Then a genuine, low-pressure ask to connect or learn more, with a soft acknowledgement that it's a bit of an ask from a stranger. Warm and direct, first person. No flattery filler ('hope you're having a great week'), no buzzwords, no em dashes.
note_must_include: the specific angle or detail that made you reach out (their transition, project, role, or what the company/team is building)
a brief low-pressure close (e.g. 'no worries if it's too much')
note_must_avoid: I hope this finds you well
I am looking for a job
outreach.note_ask: Connect, or an open invite to hear about their journey/team - no CV attachment, no explicit job ask, no link, in the first note.
outreach.note_example: Hi James, your move from healthcare into data stood out to me. I'd love to hear about that journey. No worries if this is a big ask from a stranger!
outreach.note_monthly_limit_label: 5 notes per month (LinkedIn free-plan limit on personalized invites)
outreach.followup_auto_send_label: Draft only - you send it yourself from the dashboard
outreach.followup_tone: Short, genuine, references what you noticed in the note they accepted. Ask about their team's data stack or how the role came about - one open, low-pressure question. No direct 'do you have a job for me' in follow-up 1.
outreach.about_me_label: Positioning line: what you do, in one sentence (blank = messages stay company-only)
outreach.followup_2_tone: 4 days after follow-up 1, shorter, a friendly reminder that closes the loop gracefully.
outreach.candidates_to_inspect_label: Open the top 4 matching profiles per role and pick the best-qualified one (never message all of them)
outreach.peer_enabled_label: On - also connect with 1 peer per company (someone on the team you'd join)

peer_tier.who: Data Analyst, BI Analyst, Analytics Engineer, Data Engineer - an individual contributor on the team you'd join, not a manager or recruiter

outreach.peer_common_ground_label: Same department (data) always; add your university / background / past companies to find stronger matches
outreach.peer_ask: A 15-minute chat about what the team works on and what they look for in new people - never a referral or job ask in the first note.
outreach.peer_note_example: Hi Nino, fellow data person here - I build scraping pipelines and Power BI reporting. Would love 15 min to hear how the data team at Acme works. No worries if not!
outreach.peer_followup_tone: Thank them for connecting, name the common ground, then ask for a 15-minute call about the team and how they got in. Casual, peer-to-peer, no pitch link. Follow-up 2: after a call, or if they replied warmly, ask if there is anyone else on the team worth talking to, or whether they would be open to referring you for a matching role.
outreach.pitch_link_label: Not set yet - CV / video pitch link (e.g. Reslink) for the first message after acceptance
outreach.cv_attachment_label: Not set - path to a CV PDF to attach to the first message after acceptance
outreach.no_accept_email_days_label: If a request is still unaccepted after 5 days, draft an email for you to send
outreach.emails_per_run_label: Draft at most 10 fallback emails per run (newest unaccepted requests first)
outreach.email_tone: Short cold email, under 120 words. Subject line names the role or team. Body: who you are in one line ({about_me}), the specific reason you picked their company, the ask matched to their role (recruiter: whether you could be considered for data roles; hiring manager: whether that work is something the team is bringing on; peer: a 15-minute chat), and {pitch_link} if set. Mention you also sent a LinkedIn request. No em dashes.

job_contacts.who: The person the analyst role reports to, in the job's department: e.g. Healthcare Analytics Manager, Head of Product Analytics, Marketing Analytics Lead, Data/BI Manager for that team
The recruiter or talent partner who hires for that department or for data/analytics roles - ideally the one who posted this job

outreach.job_contacts_label: Per job: the department's hiring manager + the recruiter for that department (falls back to general data manager / recruiter / talent acquisition)
outreach.job_note_example: Hi Sarah, saw Acme is hiring a Product Analyst for the healthcare team. I work with SQL, Python and Power BI and would love to connect about the role. No worries if not!
outreach.job_followup_tone: Short, under 350 characters, the message the user asked for: (1) thanks for connecting; (2) one line on who you are, from {about_me}; (3) you are reaching out about the <job_title> role at <company>; (4) 'here is my CV: {pitch_link}' (if pitch_link is blank: 'happy to send my CV'); (5) you would really appreciate any feedback, or a pointer to the right person. Warm, plain, first person, no em dashes, never 'do you have a job for me'.
outreach.job_followup_2_tone: 4 days after the first message, under 200 characters: a friendly one-line reminder about the <job_title> role and the CV link, thanking them either way.

custom_fields_added: job_id, job_title, job_url, job_location, job_workplace, job_department, job_posted, location_eligibility, cv_fit
